Since both orbit periods are retained, the deck transformations fix the orbit coordinates, commute with the orbit flows, and preserve each reflected section and its orientation. Lemma~\ref{lem:free-section-displacements} therefore gives a nowhere-zero horizontal Killing field on $X$ with integrable orthogonal distribution. Finally, Lemma~\ref{lem:properness-static-field} forces $\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_\infty$ to be flat, contradicting $|\mathrm{Rm}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_\infty)|(p)=1$.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{prop:bounded-density}
Let $(X,\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}})$ be a connected complete four-manifold with Killing fields $K_1,K_2$ satisfying
\[
\operatorname{Ric}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}})=0,\qquad [K_1,K_2]=0,\qquad \ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}(K_1,K_2)=0.
\]
Set $\rho:=|K_1\wedge K_2|_\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}$. Suppose $\{\rho>0\}$ is dense and the distribution $\operatorname{span}\{K_1,K_2\}^{\perp}$ is integrable there. Let $h$ denote the local quotient metric on this set, and assume
\[
\sup_X\rho<\infty,\qquad K_h\leq0.
\]
Then $\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}$ is flat.
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
On $\{\rho>0\}$, where $\ensuremath{\text{d}}\rho\neq0$, follow the unit gradient $e=\nabla\rho/|\ensuremath{\text{d}}\rho|$ and let $e^\perp$ be a horizontal unit normal to it. Equations~\eqref{eqn:general-horizontal}--\eqref{eqn:general-trace} and Remark~\ref{rem:diagonal-reduction} give
\begin{eqnarray*}
\nabla_\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}^2\rho(e,e)
=\rho\left(-K_h+\tfrac12\ensuremath{\text{d}} u(e^\perp)^2\right)\geq0.
\end{eqnarray*}
Thus along its integral curve, $\rho'=|\ensuremath{\text{d}}\rho|>0$ and $\rho''\geq0$. The functions $\rho$ and $|\ensuremath{\text{d}}\rho|$ stay bounded below by positive constants. If the curve had a finite maximal forward time, its unit speed and completeness would give a limit point in the independent, noncritical locus, where the unit gradient field is smooth; the curve would therefore extend. Thus it exists for all positive time, and $\rho(\gamma(t))\geq\rho(\gamma(0))+t|\ensuremath{\text{d}}\rho(\gamma(0))|$, contrary to boundedness. Hence $\ensuremath{\text{d}}\rho=0$ on $\{\rho>0\}$. Equation~\eqref{eqn:general-horizontal} reduces to $K_hh=\tfrac12\ensuremath{\text{d}} u\otimes\ensuremath{\text{d}} u$ and forces $K_h=0$ and $\ensuremath{\text{d}} u=0$. By Remark~\ref{rem:diagonal-reduction}, the metric is a flat product there, and density of this set gives flatness everywhere.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:curvature-noncollapse}
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that every Einstein metric $\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}\in\mathcal X_\beta$, with $\beta\in I$, has $|{\rm Rm}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}})|_\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}\leq C$ on $S^4\setminus\mathcal T$ and ${\rm Vol}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}})\geq 64 \pi^2 / C^2$.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
Suppose the curvature bound fails. Choose $q_i=|\text{Rm}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i)|(p_i)\geq\tfrac12\sup|\text{Rm}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i)|\to\infty$, and rescale by $\widetilde\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i=q_i\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i$ as per Notation \ref{not:rescaled-covers}. Propositions~\ref{prop:noedgebubble} and~\ref{prop:no-collapsed-smooth-limit}, followed by the smooth compactness argument of Lemma~\ref{lem:marked-compactness}, give a complete smooth Ricci-flat limit with $|\text{Rm}|(p_\infty)=1$. Lemma~\ref{lem:quotient-curvature} gives $K_{h_\infty}\leq0$. Proposition~\ref{prop:polarbubbles} gives a compact edge $E_\infty$, identified with an entire original edge $E_i$. Primitive periods and both endpoints are preserved. Set $P_i:=P(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i)$, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:density}. Let $b_i$ be the length, in the rescaled metric, of the generator that does not vanish on $E_i$. The expansion~\eqref{eqn:edge-slice-expansion} gives $\partial_\nu\rho=b$. Combining this with~\eqref{eq:density-boundary} and smooth equivariant convergence along the entire edge, with the primitive generators unchanged, gives
\begin{eqnarray*}
\frac{q_iP_i}{2}
=-\int_{E_i}*_{h_i}\ensuremath{\text{d}}\widetilde\rho_i
=\int_{E_i}b_i\,\ensuremath{\text{d}} s_i
\longrightarrow\int_{E_\infty}b_\infty\,\ensuremath{\text{d}} s_\infty\in(0,\infty).
\end{eqnarray*}
Thus $q_iP_i$ is bounded. Lemma~\ref{lem:density} bounds $\widetilde\rho_i=q_i\rho_i$, and hence the limiting density. By Lemma~\ref{prop:bounded-density}, the limit is flat, a contradiction. With $|\text{Rm}|\leq C$, \eqref{eqn:L2-bound} gives $64\pi^2\leq C^2 {\rm Vol}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}})$.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{lem:cone-separation-trace}
There exist constants $d_0>0$ and $0<a_0\leq a_1<\infty$ such that every Einstein metric $\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}\in\mathcal X_\beta$, with $\beta\in I$, satisfies
\[
\operatorname{dist}_{\hat\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}}(c,\partial\Sigma)\geq d_0,
\qquad a_0\leq\rho(c)\leq a_1.
\]
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Take $C$ from Proposition~\ref{prop:curvature-noncollapse}, $D=\pi\sqrt{3/\lambda}$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:global-bounds} and set $V_{\text{min}} = 64 \pi^2 / C^2$. Set $l:=\operatorname{dist}_{\hat\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}}(c,\partial\Sigma)$. Along a shortest quotient geodesic from $c$ to the boundary, choose a generator vanishing at the endpoint. Its length $\phi$ satisfies $\phi''+C\phi\geq0$, $\phi(0)>0$, $\phi'(0)=0$, and $\phi(l)=0$. For $t<\min\{l,\pi/(2\sqrt C)\}$, comparison gives $\phi(t)\geq\phi(0)\cos(\sqrt Ct)>0$. Hence its first zero cannot occur before $d_0=\pi/(2\sqrt C)$, so $l\geq d_0$. Minimizing geodesics from $c$ to interior points avoid the boundary as in Lemma~\ref{lem:density-maximum}. Since $K_{\hat g}\geq-C$, polar comparison, integrated up to the cut time, gives
\begin{eqnarray*}
\operatorname{Area}_{\hat\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}}(\Sigma)
\leq2\pi\beta\int_0^D\frac{\sinh(\sqrt Ct)}{\sqrt C}\ensuremath{\text{d}} t
\leq\frac{2\pi}{C}(\cosh(\sqrt CD)-1)=:A_0.
\end{eqnarray*}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:density-maximum} and~\eqref{eq:orbit-volume}, $V_{\text{min}}\leq4\pi^2\rho(c)A_0$. This gives $a_0=V_{\text{min}}/(4\pi^2A_0)$. The upper bound follows from Lemmas~\ref{lem:density} and~\ref{lem:global-bounds}.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:compact-zero-set}
For every compact interval $I\subset(0,1/2]$, the total zero set
\[
\mathscr Z_I:=\{(\beta,\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}})\in\mathcal X_I: {\rm Ric}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}) = \lambda \ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}\}
\]
is compact.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
We first obtain geometric convergence, then recover the prescribed conformal coordinates. Take a sequence $(\beta_i,\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i)\in\mathscr Z_I$ and pass to a subsequence with $\beta_i\to\beta_\infty\in I$. Proposition~\ref{prop:curvature-noncollapse} and Lemma~\ref{lem:global-bounds} bound curvature and diameter above and volume below. Bishop comparison on the complete $\mathrm{RCD}(\lambda,4)$ spaces gives a uniform lower bound for the volume of every fixed-radius ball. At any fixed positive distance from $\mathcal T$, the local Cheeger--Gromov--Taylor estimate~\cite[Theorem~4.3]{CheegerGromovTaylor} therefore bounds the injectivity radius below. In uniformly controlled harmonic charts, elliptic estimates for the Einstein equation~\cite[\S5]{DeTurckKazdan1981} give bounds for all derivatives on smaller charts, and hence smooth subsequential convergence away from the cone~\cite[Chapter~11]{petersen2016riemannian}.

Each of the two fixed circle generators $K_a$ vanishes on its axis with $|\nabla K_a|=\sqrt2$. The estimate $|\nabla^2K_a|\leq C|\mathrm{Rm}|\,|K_a|$ and the diameter bound give uniform bounds for $K_a$ and $\nabla K_a$ by transport from its axis. Apply the averaging construction in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:properness-marked-action} also to $\Gamma$ and the coordinate conjugations $\kappa_j$. The resulting convergence is equivariant, preserves the primitive generators and labelled axes, and identifies the meridional sections. Lemma~\ref{lem:cone-separation-trace} separates the cone from the boundary and bounds its orbit-area density above and below, while Lemma~\ref{lem:normalized-cone-charts} supplies normalized isothermal cone charts on a common disk.

We recover the conformal marking on the global section $S=S_\Sigma^2$, using the reflections $\eta_1,\eta_2$ and the four-point set $C$ of \S\ref{sec:scalar_eqn_function_spaces}. Also write $\hat\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i$ for the reflected quotient metric on $S$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:slice-regularity}, it is smooth across the axes and at the vertices, where four right-angle quadrants meet. The six points $p_\pm$ and $C$ remain distinct. Indeed, a uniform equivariant normal ball about a torus fixed point contains no other fixed point, since its isotropy representation has no fixed vector; the injectivity estimates therefore separate the vertices. The cone-separation bound separates the four lifts of $c$ from the axes and hence from each other.

Since the section is totally geodesic, restrictions of ambient exponential charts give uniform normal charts on $S$ away from the four cone points, including at the axes and vertices. Smooth compactness on the complements of four smaller cone disks, followed by attaching the limiting disks, gives a limiting section diffeomorphic to $S$. Choose a finite conformal atlas consisting of ordinary isothermal disks and normalized cone disks at the four points of $C$. In a cone disk,
\[
\hat\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i=e^{2v_i}|\zeta|^{2\beta_i-2}|\ensuremath{\text{d}}\zeta|^2;
\]
the scalar factor does not affect the conformal structure, which extends across the center in the coordinate $\zeta$. Take disjoint disks about the six marked points and arrange that all overlaps avoid their centers. Smooth convergence on the regular part and the normalized cone estimates give corresponding charts on common smaller domains, with transition maps converging smoothly on the overlaps.

Use the geometric identifications off the marked disks and the exact coordinate identifications on smaller disks about their centers. On the intervening annuli, the maps are $\mathcal C^1$-close and can be joined using cutoff functions in common target coordinate charts. For large $i$ the resulting maps are local diffeomorphisms, hence diffeomorphisms because the surfaces are compact and the target is a sphere. They identify the sections with one fixed sphere and preserve the marked points. In these identifications, the Beltrami coefficients relative to the limiting conformal structure converge uniformly to zero: they vanish on the smaller marked disks, and smooth convergence controls the complement.

Let $c_*\in C$ be the lift in the chamber $r_1,r_2\geq0$. As in Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-marking}, uniformize the sections by maps $W_i$ satisfying
\[
W_i(p_-)=0,\qquad W_i(p_+)=\infty,\qquad W_i(c_*)=1.
\]
The normalized maps and their inverses converge uniformly to a biholomorphism $W_\infty$ and its inverse~\cite[Theorems~8--9 and Lemma~18]{AhlforsBers}. In the corresponding local holomorphic charts, Cauchy's estimates give convergence of all derivatives on smaller disks. In particular, the limiting chart transitions have nonzero first derivatives.

To recover the marking of Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-marking}, set $\iota:=\eta_1\eta_2$. This holomorphic involution fixes $p_\pm$ and is nontrivial, so $W_i\circ\iota=-W_i$. Consequently,
\[
Z_i=iW_i^2
\]
descends to $S/\langle\iota\rangle=\widehat\Sigma$ and satisfies $Z_i(p_-)=0$, $Z_i(p_+)=\infty$, and $Z_i(c_+)=i$. Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-marking} gives $Z_i(c_-)=-i$ and identifies $Z_i$ with the prescribed normalization. Since each $\hat\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i$ is conformal to the fixed round structure, this recovers exactly the original conformal coordinates, with their labelled reflection axes and $\Gamma$ symmetries. Keeping the orbit angles fixed extends these identifications smoothly across axes and corners, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:slice-regularity} and the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:ambient-einstein-regularity}.

For the holomorphic transition $z=\phi_i(\zeta)$ from a normalized cone chart to the fixed local chart, we have $\phi_i(0)=0$ and $\phi_i'(0)\to\phi_\infty'(0)\ne0$. Comparing leading normal coefficients gives
\[
1=a_{0,i}|\phi_i'(0)|^{2\beta_i},\qquad
a_{0,i}\longrightarrow|\phi_\infty'(0)|^{-2\beta_\infty}>0.
\]
The common leading orbit coefficient is $b_{0,i}=\rho_i(c)$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:cone-separation-trace} gives a subsequence with a positive limit for $b_{0,i}$. All these coefficients are measured against the original primitive generators.

Choose $\delta<\delta'<\min\{1,2\beta_0\}$, $m>k+2$, and $\alpha<\alpha'<1$. Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-cone-estimates} bounds the normalized remainders in $x^{\delta'}\mathcal C_b^{m,\alpha'}$. The holomorphic transitions and their inverses converge smoothly on common smaller disks with first derivatives bounded away from zero. Thus the same bounds hold in the fixed chart: the two radial variables are uniformly comparable, and the smooth correction to the leading normal factor is $O(x)$, which is allowed since $\delta'<1$. Since~\eqref{eq:angle-identification} leaves the scalar coefficients unchanged, Lemma~\ref{lem:compactness}, together with smooth convergence on the compact complement, gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:properness-topology}
\mathcal I_{\beta_i}\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_i\longrightarrow\mathcal I_{\beta_\infty}\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_\infty
\quad\text{in }\mathcal S_{1/2}^{k+2,\alpha}.
\end{equation}
The geometric limit is positive away from $\mathcal T$, and the limiting leading coefficients are positive. The defining tensor form and symmetries are closed conditions, so $\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_\infty\in\mathcal X_{\beta_\infty}$. The Einstein equation passes to the limit under local $\mathcal C^2$ convergence away from $\mathcal T$, giving $\operatorname{Ric}(\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_\infty)=\lambda\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_\infty$. Hence $\mathscr Z_I$ is compact.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{lem:half-angle-zero}
The section $\mathcal R_{1/2}$ has exactly one zero in $\mathcal M$. Its corresponding metric $\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_{1/2}\in\mathcal X_{1/2}$ is the quotient of the equal round product on $S^2\times S^2$ by simultaneous reflection across the two equators.
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:scalar-zero-equivalence}, it suffices to prove existence and uniqueness of the Einstein metric in $\mathcal X_{1/2}$. Let $a_j$ reflect the $j$th factor across its equator, and let $S$ exchange the factors. On the quotient by $a_1a_2$, use the coordinates $\zeta=(s_1+is_2)^2$, $\vartheta_1$, and $\vartheta_2$ near the image of the fixed torus. The orbit space of this smooth closed four-manifold is the latitude square modulo $(s_1,s_2)\mapsto(-s_1,-s_2)$: a disk with two corners, primitive edge labels $e_1,e_2$, and no exceptional orbits. The equivariant reconstruction theorem~\cite[\S4.2, p.~546]{OrlikRaymond1} identifies it with the fixed $S^4$ action, sending the central orbit to $\mathcal T$.

Near that orbit,
\[
 \hat\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_P=(4\lambda)^{-1}|\zeta|^{-1}|\ensuremath{\text{d}}\zeta|^2,
 \qquad e^f=\lambda^{-1}\cos s_1\cos s_2,
 \qquad u=\log(\cos s_1/\cos s_2).
\]
The normalized conformal identification of Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-marking} intertwines the descended $S,a_1$ with $\sigma,\tau$. Keeping the orbit angles unchanged extends it smoothly across axes and corners by reflection. At the cone, $\zeta=Az+O(z^2)$ with $A\ne0$, so
\[
 \hat\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_P=\frac{|A|}{4\lambda}|z|^{-1}(1+O_b(|z|))|\ensuremath{\text{d}} z|^2,
 \qquad f+\log\lambda,u=O_b(|z|).
\]
Thus the cone angle is $\pi$ and $v-v_0=O_b(x)$, where $v_0=\tfrac12\log(|A|/(4\lambda))$. Since $\delta<1$, Lemma~\ref{lem:decay-implies-little} places these remainders in $x^\delta c_b^{k+2,\alpha}$, so the quotient lies in $\mathcal X_{1/2}$.

Conversely, Proposition~\ref{prop:removability} lifts any Einstein metric in $\mathcal X_{1/2}$ to $S^2\times S^2$, where Theorem~\ref{thm:product-page-uniqueness} identifies it with the equal round product. Conjugate its torus action to the product rotation action. The induced torus automorphism preserves the two primitive stabilizer subgroups, so it is a signed permutation. Product isometries absorb these changes of basis. The deck involution commutes with both rotation circles and fixes the ramification torus; it therefore reflects both factors across their equators and equals $a_1a_2$.

The descended isometry has the form $(q,\vartheta)\mapsto(\phi(q),\vartheta+\psi(q))$. The absence of mixed quotient--orbit terms gives $\ensuremath{\text{d}}\psi=0$; a constant torus translation makes $\psi=0$. Compose with $\tau$, if necessary, to fix both corners. Then $\phi$ preserves orientation and each labelled edge. Its holomorphic double fixes the three normalized points, so Lemma~\ref{lem:fixed-marking} gives $\phi=\mathrm{id}$.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:half-angle-degree}
The derivative
\[
 \mathrm D_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_{1/2}}\mathcal R_{1/2}:
 T_{\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_{1/2}}\mathcal M\longrightarrow\mathcal Z_{1/2,\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_{1/2}}
\]
is an isomorphism, and $\deg_2(\mathcal R_{1/2})=1$.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Let $(\phi,\psi,\chi)$ belong to the kernel. Proposition~\ref{prop:scalar-zero-equivalence} identifies its metric variation with an infinitesimal Einstein deformation, with ambient $c^{k+2,\alpha}$ regularity at the axes and vertices. Denote its pullback to the round product by $H$.

At the branch locus, use $z=w^2$ and put $R=|w|$. Write $f,u$ for the smooth lifted background functions and $\hat\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_P=e^{2V}|\ensuremath{\text{d}} w|^2$. The pulled-back scalar variations satisfy
\[
 \begin{split}
 \Delta_w\phi+2\langle\ensuremath{\text{d}} f,\ensuremath{\text{d}}\phi\rangle
                         +4\lambda e^{2V}\chi&=0,\\
 \Delta_w\psi+\langle\ensuremath{\text{d}} f,\ensuremath{\text{d}}\psi\rangle
                         +\langle\ensuremath{\text{d}} u,\ensuremath{\text{d}}\phi\rangle&=0,\\
 \Delta_w\chi-\tfrac12\langle\ensuremath{\text{d}} f,\ensuremath{\text{d}}\phi\rangle
                         +\tfrac12\langle\ensuremath{\text{d}} u,\ensuremath{\text{d}}\psi\rangle&=0,
 \end{split}
\]
where the inner products are Euclidean. Their defining asymptotics give
\[
 (\phi,\psi,\chi)=(\phi_0,0,\chi_0)+O(R^{2\delta}),
 \qquad |D_w(\phi,\psi,\chi)|=O(R^{2\delta-1}).
\]
Since $\delta>0$, these functions lie locally in $W^{1,2}$ and their boundary flux on $R=\eta$ is $O(\eta^{2\delta})$. Integration by parts therefore extends the equations weakly across $w=0$. Elliptic regularity makes the variations smooth there. Hence $H$ is a $c^{k+2,\alpha}$ infinitesimal Einstein deformation on the whole product.

\phantomsection\label{notloc:gauge-conventions}
Use $(\delta H)_j=-\nabla^iH_{ij}$ and $\delta^*X=\tfrac12\mathcal L_X\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_P$. The elliptic self-adjoint operator $\delta\delta^*$ has the Killing fields as its kernel. Since $\langle\delta H,K\rangle_{L^2}=\langle H,\delta^*K\rangle_{L^2}=0$ for every Killing field $K$, solve
\[
 \delta\delta^*X=\delta H,
 \qquad X\in c^{k+3,\alpha}.
\]
Average over the torus, the two circle-coordinate conjugations, and the deck involution. They preserve $H$ and $\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}_P$, so the averaged field still solves the equation and is horizontal. Then $H_0=H-\delta^*X$ is divergence-free and satisfies the linearized Einstein equation.

Its trace $t$ satisfies $\Delta t+\lambda t=0$. Bochner's identity gives
\[
 \int|\nabla^2t|^2\,\ensuremath{\text{d}} V
 =\int(\Delta t)^2\,\ensuremath{\text{d}} V-\lambda\int|\ensuremath{\text{d}} t|^2\,\ensuremath{\text{d}} V=0,
\]
so $t$ is constant and hence zero. The transverse-traceless Einstein equation is elliptic, making $H_0$ smooth. Koiso's classification~\cite[Theorem~5.7, pp.~659--660]{Koiso82} gives no nonzero transverse-traceless infinitesimal Einstein deformations of the equal round product. Thus $H=\delta^*X$.

The common fixed surface $T$ of the two circle-coordinate conjugations is a product of great circles, with a flat metric. The averaged field $X$ is tangent to $T$. Since the horizontal part of $H$ is conformal to the quotient metric, $X|_T$ is a conformal vector field on this flat torus. Its components satisfy the Cauchy--Riemann equations and are therefore constant. In global arclength coordinates on $T$, the deck involution acts by $(s_1,s_2)\mapsto(-s_1,-s_2)$, so invariance forces this constant field to vanish. Every torus orbit meets $T$; torus invariance gives $X=0$, hence $H=0$ and $(\phi,\psi,\chi)=0$.

Theorem~\ref{thm:scalar-index-zero} now makes the derivative an isomorphism. Lemma~\ref{lem:half-angle-zero} and Proposition~\ref{prop:localized-degree} give $\deg_2(\mathcal R_{1/2})=1$.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
Choose $d=m+1$ and $I=[\beta_0,1/2]$, with $0<\beta_0<1/d$. By Propositions~\ref{prop:scalar-zero-equivalence} and~\ref{prop:removability}, it suffices to find a zero of $\mathcal R_{1/d}$ in $\mathcal M$. We show, more generally, that $\mathcal R_\beta$ has a zero for every $\beta\in I$.

Theorems~\ref{thm:scalar-index-zero} and~\ref{thm:compact-zero-set} give the Fredholm index-zero property and compactness of the total zero set. Applying Proposition~\ref{prop:localized-degree} with the projections of Remark~\ref{rem:scalar-degree-projections}, homotopy invariance gives
\[
 \deg_2(\mathcal R_\beta)
 =\deg_2(\mathcal R_{1/2})=1
 \qquad\text{for every }\beta\in I,
\]
where the last equality follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:half-angle-degree}. Nonzero degree implies that $\mathcal R_\beta$ has a zero. In particular, a zero at $\beta=1/d$ determines an Einstein metric $\ensuremath{\mathrm{g}}\in\mathcal X_{1/d}$, whose pullback by $p_{d-1}$ extends to a smooth Einstein metric with $\lambda>0$ on $\sharp_m(S^2\times S^2)$, with the effective isometric $\ensuremath{\mathsf{T}^2}$-action constructed in $\S$\ref{sec:branched-cover}.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
